name: @local/dsh-oks
description: A Harness capability, not a wrapper for one model: whatever knowledge service (OKS) and data file a session's workspace declares in oks.json become twelve native tools — search / references / info / check_intent / query / create_data / jq_transform / jq_transform_into / chart / view / report / artifacts — turning a business question into rows read from that data file over a read-only connection, and into figures drawn on the server as SVG files in the workspace. oks_check_intent validates named intents and hands back a key for each accepted one; oks_query re-hashes that key before running, saves every success into a result file under the workspace's .oks/data/, and returns only its dataSrc, columns and row count — the rows stay out of the model context until jq_transform reads them with a jaq/jq expression over named inputs (each input may be any product, read in place with no intermediate file, and root picks which slice of it the snip gets: .data by default, .origin for the source chain, .meta or the whole file; a jq program's value stream is collected uniformly: one value is that value, several are an array, none is an empty array), and jq_transform_into materialises a result as a new file whose origin carries this operation (snip, motivation, output count) plus the complete source chain of every input, without the inputs' own data; create_data does the same for data the agent supplies itself, so that supplied numbers carry a recorded reason and can be referenced like anything else. oks_chart draws a figure — columns, bars, lines, areas, pie, scatter, histogram, box, heatmap or radar, rendered by echarts — into an SVG file in the workspace, taking its rows from a saved envelope only (src: queried rows, a computed result, or rows created with create_data — never inline), embedding the rows it drew, its specification and the whole source chain in the SVG, and returning the markdown line that shows the figure in the reply. Every file is { meta, origin, data }: meta says what it is (kind, name, time, and for figures and reports a title and category), origin is the operation that produced the data together with its complete upstream source chain written as a node table inside the file, and data is that data itself (what jq sees by default); the shape is recognized structurally, with no version number. Search finds the keys of the vocabulary by name or description, references walks the reference graph backwards, and oks_info reads any node from the opaque key "index". va_ask consults a vocabulary helper the plugin owns (a top-level agent on the same preset and workspace, sharing the process-wide index, archived while idle): the plugin prepares it in one shot by putting the whole vocabulary and the working method into its system prompt — assembly sends no message at all — and after every answer collapses the question-and-answer into one fixed-text marker, so between questions the helper sees only the vocabulary, the method and the current question, while the session log stays append-only. oks_view turns saved data into a markdown display piece (.oks/views/ — a table you can open and read, with its source chain and final data hidden in a leading HTML comment), which renders both in the reply and inside a report. oks_report assembles several figures, tables and prose into one self-contained HTML report — figures inlined as SVG, tables as real <table> elements, with a table of contents and captions, and a report-level provenance structure holding each display item's final data and whole source chain (it fails outright when a referenced material is missing or the provenance grows past its cap); a report's display items and any product's source chain are read with the same jq_transform, because root can hand over .origin instead of .data — reading data and reading provenance are one path, with no dedicated tool and no cross-check of the recorded data file. An HTML report is handed over with the present tool and read in the sidebar, not in the reply body. Reports are temporary by default: an unpinned one is removed about an hour after it was produced, and the internal materials (data and figures) are reclaimed on the same schedule; the user decides what to keep with a pin in the sidebar, and oks_artifacts lists what exists. Reports live in artifacts/, internal materials and the state that knows what is pinned live in .oks/.
